description: This 1992 Dodge Stealth R/T Turbo is a two-door performance coupe from the early years of the model. It uses the R/T Turbo designation associated with the higher-output versions of the Stealth line, and it carries the design and engineering approach Dodge used for this period of Japanese-market-influenced sports cars. The body has a low profile with a long hood, a short rear deck, and integrated aerodynamic shaping that was part of the car's original form. Its exterior surfaces are clean and angular, with pop-up headlamp styling characteristic of the era. The proportions are compact, and the glass area, roofline, and beltline all follow the same purposeful theme that defined many performance coupes of the early 1990s.Power comes from a turbocharged engine, which is central to the R/T Turbo model designation. This drivetrain was intended to provide stronger acceleration than the naturally aspirated versions in the same family. The turbocharging hardware adds complexity to the engine package and is one of the key mechanical distinctions of this trim. The power delivery in these cars was known for combining low-end drivability with additional pull as boost builds, and that character is part of what made the model relevant in its segment. This vehicle's performance identity is tied to that engine choice more than to any decorative element, and the mechanical specification is the main point of interest for anyone evaluating it.This example includes Premium Audio. That equipment indicates a higher-level sound system than the base installation, and it adds to the car's interior specification without changing the vehicle's core mechanical character. The cabin of the Stealth R/T Turbo was arranged around front-seat occupants, with controls and instrumentation positioned for the driver in a manner consistent with performance-oriented coupes of the time. Materials, switchgear, and trim details varied by market and equipment level, but the overall treatment was aimed at a more substantial presentation than a bare entry model. The premium sound option sits within that framework and reflects how this car was ordered when new, alongside the other factory equipment rather than as an aftermarket addition.This example also includes Fog Lights. That exterior feature was offered as part of the car's equipment list and is visible as a separate lighting detail at the front of the body. It is one of the few added items specifically identified for this vehicle, and it fits the Stealth's original design without altering the overall shape. The 1992 model year places this car within the first generation of the Stealth, when Dodge was using this platform to present a more technical, contemporary sports coupe with a turbocharged engine and a restrained interior specification. The combination of the R/T Turbo trim with the listed options keeps the focus on factory content rather than modification, and the car remains defined by the hardware and equipment it was built with from the outset.
